title: The Morpho pool collateralized by Sky's own sUSDS is the only one given an unlimited absolute cap
content:
Among the four Morpho pools listed at A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.4.3.1.1.4.1, exactly one has `Absolute cap: Unlimited`: the **sUSDS/USDT 96.5% LLTV** pool (.4.1.1). The three pools backed by external collateral — wstETH, WBTC, cbBTC, all at 86% LLTV — carry hard notional caps.

Two parameters move together here. The uncapped pool also has by far the most aggressive liquidation threshold: 96.5% LLTV versus 86%. Higher LLTV means a thinner buffer before a position is underwater, so the pool with the *least* collateral cushion is the one with the *most* size permitted.

The consistent reading is that sUSDS is treated as near-riskless because Sky issues it: its value is a function of Sky's own solvency, not of an external market's price action. Lending USDT against sUSDS is close to lending against your own liability, so both a tight LLTV and an unbounded size look defensible.

The implication is a correlated risk that the two-dimensional cap structure does not capture. External-collateral exposures are bounded and diversified; sUSDS exposure is unbounded and perfectly correlated with the issuer. If sUSDS ever depegs, the one pool with no size limit and the smallest buffer is the one that fails — and it fails for the same reason the rest of Sky is already in trouble.
description: sUSDS/USDT at 96.5% LLTV has no notional ceiling while wstETH, WBTC and cbBTC pools are capped at 250M/100M — self-referential collateral is treated as the least risky exposure.
